Article Title: 'We stand ready': China signals push to ease business visa process for Indians amid reported curbs

NEW DELHI: China on Monday said it was ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both countries, amid reports of a slowdown in visa issuance to Indian nationals."China issues visas for eligible foreign nationals coming to China in accordance with laws and regulations," a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said in a written response to questions from news agency PTI."We stand ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel of both sides," the spokesperson added.The remarks come amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business travellers.According to PTI, fewer Indian businessmen were reportedly granted visas to attend this month's China International Import Expo in Shanghai. The annual trade fair provides a platform for businesses from around the world to showcase their products to Chinese consumers.Beijing has also stopped the China Visa Application Centre, a service provider, from accepting visa applications, with Chinese diplomatic missions now handling them directly amid rising demand for visas, particularly business visas.Visa arrangements between the two countries have improved since India resumed issuing tourist visas to Chinese nationals in July last year after a gap of five years. The move was part of efforts to repair bilateral ties, which came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020.The resumption of tourist visas was seen as a significant step towards normalising relations after years of strained ties.As part of efforts to ease travel, the two countries also resumed direct air connectivity between several cities, including the Beijing-New Delhi route.According to Indian officials, the visa rejection rate for Chinese nationals has come down to around seven per cent in recent months to encourage business and tourism-related travel to India.China, meanwhile, launched the "China Online Visa Application System" for Indian applicants in December last year, allowing them to apply for visas online.Responding to a question on the status of bilateral relations following a meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Brics summit in New Delhi in September this year, the spokesperson said Beijing was ready to work with New Delhi to strengthen ties."The most important common understanding they (PM Modi and Xi) reached is that China and India need to be partners. Both sides are working to deliver on this important common understanding."China stands ready to work with India to improve and grow bilateral relations, support each other's development and revitalisation, and contribute to world peace and prosperity," the spokesperson said.
Article Summary: China says it is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both countries. Comments come amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals. India resumed issuing tourist visas to Chinese nationals in July last year after a gap of five years.

Article Title: 'Couldn't even fill single Ramlila Maidan': BJP's Nitin Nabin takes jibe at Rahul's 'vote chori' rally
Article Text:
Nitin Nabin hits out at Rahul Gandhi over 'vote chori' allegations

Nabin targets INDIA bloc over vote theft allegations

NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Monday targeted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his 'vote chori' allegations, claiming the INDIA bloc had failed to fill even a single Ramlila Maidan during its rally in Delhi. Addressing a BJP rally in Karimnagar, Telangana , Nabin said BJP workers had drawn larger crowds across more than 200 locations and accused Rahul of advocating for alleged infiltrators to be included in voter lists."Rahul Gandhi ji used to say that vote chori took place. Rahul ji, the people are with us, and the votes are with us. The people of Karimnagar have shown that their blessings are with us. They (the INDIA alliance), despite putting in their all, couldn't even fill a single Ramlila Maidan, while BJP workers gathered far more people than could fit in a Ramlila Maidan at over 200 locations," news agency ANI quoted him as saying.Nabin also questioned Rahul Gandhi's claim that 13 crore votes had been stolen and challenged his stand on the inclusion of people whose whereabouts were allegedly unverified."Rahul ji claimed that 13 crore people's votes had been stolen. But I would like to ask: Why should 3 crore people be included in the voter list? More than 6 crore people have shifted. I know that in Telangana, lakhs of people have shifted their votes.So, should people be allowed to vote twice? The remaining 3 crore are those whose whereabouts the Election Commission enquired about in 2003, but they have no answers. So, the person advocating for these 3 crore infiltrators is none other than Rahul Gandhi," he said.The BJP chief accused opposition parties of attempting to create chaos, while asserting that the BJP was receiving public support through democratic means."They tried to spread chaos—let them have their chaos! We, on the other hand, are receiving democracy's blessings," Nabin said.Taking a swipe at Rahul Gandhi's references to the Constitution, he said, "I have come to tell those who carry a copy of the Constitution around in their hands: you have a copy of the Constitution in your hands, but the Constitution is in our hearts. You speak of the Constitution, but we revere it. That is why we respect all constitutional institutions."He also invoked the Emergency to target the Congress, saying, "The people who murdered democracy by imposing the Emergency to save their own seats are today invoking democracy."Nabin also criticised Rahul Gandhi's remarks on India's economy, accusing him of insulting the country both within India and abroad."Whenever Rahul Gandhi is in the country, he does nothing but insult it, and he insults it abroad too. Rahul ji goes everywhere saying that India's economy is a disaster. Rahul ji, India's economy and its development are advancing on a global scale. Today, India has moved beyond the Fragile Five to become the world's fourth-largest economy," he said.Expressing confidence about the BJP's prospects in Telangana, Nabin said the party would hold the state government accountable."I am sure the countdown to the Telangana government has begun. BJP karyakartas will now hold the Telangana government accountable," he said.He also predicted that Prime Minister Narendra Modi would return to the Red Fort in 2029."Modi ji will not go anywhere; he will appear on the ramparts of the Red Fort again in 2029. Rahul ji, keep dreaming. India's youth, farmers, women, workers and people from every section of society stand with PM Modi. PM Modi is going nowhere. He will return to the ramparts of the Red Fort in 2029.Rahul ji, keep dreaming! The youth, farmers, women, workers and every section of Indian society stand with PM Modi," he said.Nabin's Telangana visit was part of the BJP's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajkata Hatao' campaign. The party has launched the campaign to counter what it describes as attempts by Congress and other opposition leaders, particularly Rahul Gandhi, to mislead people through fear, confusion and misinformation.
Article Summary: BJP national president Nitin Nabin hits out at Rahul Gandhi over 'vote chori' allegations. Nabin claims INDIA bloc failed to fill even a single Ramlila Maidan during its rally in Delhi. Accuses Rahul of advocating for alleged infiltrators to be included in voter lists.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the appellate tribunals hearing appeals related to the West Bengal Special Intensive Revision (SIR) to give preference to pleas filed by voters challenging their exclusion from the electoral rolls, while deferring those contesting the inclusion of names.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the tribunals to separate appeals challenging voter exclusions from those contesting inclusions, and give priority to the exclusions."The second set of appeals (inclusion) does not involve any urgency, and those appeals may, for the time being, be deferred. The first set of appeals (exclusions) shall be given preference in the matter of final disposal," the bench said in its order, LiveLaw reported.The bench further directed the tribunals to prioritise, within the exclusion-related appeals, cases involving voters under the jurisdiction of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, given that civic body elections are due to be held soon.The Supreme Court also directed the Election Commission (EC) to increase the number of appellate tribunals hearing appeals related to the West Bengal SIR, in consultation with the chief justice of the Calcutta high court.The top court was hearing petitions seeking steps to streamline and expedite the disposal of appeals before the tribunals set up to address grievances arising from SIR in the state.On August 25, the bench had directed the EC to submit details of pending and disposed-of appeals, with a separate count of cases filed by voters challenging their exclusion from or inclusion in the electoral rolls.The court had also asked the poll panel to specify how many additional tribunals would be needed to ensure that the appeals were decided within a stipulated timeframe.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the appellate tribunals hearing appeals related to the West Bengal Special Intensive Revision (SIR) to give preference to pleas filed by voters challenging their exclusion from the electoral rolls. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the second set of appeals (inclusion) does not involve any urgency, and those appeals may, for the time being, be deferred.

Article Title: 'Disappearing Faces': Tamannaah Bhatia, Vishal Bhardwaj discuss Sadhguru's photo book on Himalayan communities
Article Text:
Sadhguru, Tamannaah Bhatia discuss ageing, individuality and education at Mumbai event

Discussion on individuality and education

About 'Disappearing Faces'

Actor Tamannaah Bhatia and filmmaker Vishal Bhardwaj joined spiritual leader Sadhguru for a discussion on his photo book Disappearing Faces at the Fairmont Hotel in Mumbai on November 22.The conversation covered ageing, individuality, education, devotion and the changing lifestyles of people living in remote Himalayan regions.The book brings together photographs taken by Sadhguru over five decades of journeys through the Himalayas, particularly Nepal and Tibet. The portraits document people and communities whose lives have been shaped by their relationship with the natural environment.During the discussion, Tamannaah spoke about the photographs' portrayal of ageing and contrasted the acceptance of visible signs of ageing among the people captured in the book with attitudes in urban society.“Why are we not accepting of something that's the most inevitable, which is the passage of time?” she asked, observing that the people in the photographs appeared more accepting of ageing than those living in cities.Responding to her remarks, Sadhguru said attitudes towards ageing in India had changed in recent times. “This is, I think, a recent happening in India. Otherwise, women and men grew old gracefully in this country.But we have taken Western ideas where the whole civilizations are ruled by hormones,” he said.He added that society had come to place excessive importance on youth and the age associated with peak hormonal activity. “But if you make one aspect of life everything, then you will be a very skewed life,” he said.The conversation also examined the individuality of the people featured in the photographs. Tamannaah noted that despite having fewer resources, education and exposure than their urban counterparts, the people appeared to have distinct personalities and a greater sense of comfort in expressing themselves.Sadhguru linked this to the purpose of education, arguing that it was increasingly focused on preparing people for employment rather than encouraging them to explore their interests and capabilities.“Education should be about expanding our horizons,” he said, adding that many people remained occupied with securing jobs, leaving limited room to explore what they were capable of or inclined towards.Bhardwaj, meanwhile, drew attention to the stillness visible in the faces captured in the book. He referred to Sadhguru's observation that stillness represented the highest level of intensity and asked how this related to the devotional lives of saints such as Meera and Kabir.Sadhguru explained that Meera's devotion to Krishna shaped her emotional experiences, allowing her to approach everything with a sense of sweetness. Kabir, he said, sought to balance his inner experiences with the practical demands of everyday life.He also referred to Krishna as an example of being fully engaged with the world without allowing external circumstances to disturb one's inner experience.Launched in August, Disappearing Faces is a collection of photographs taken by Sadhguru during his journeys through remote Himalayan regions over five decades.The book focuses particularly on communities in Nepal and Tibet, documenting their faces, lifestyles and experiences.According to the book's description, the photographs capture ways of life that are changing with the spread of modern development and the influence of the information age.
Article Summary: Actor Tamannaah Bhatia and filmmaker Vishal Bhardwaj joined spiritual leader Sadhguru for a discussion on his photo book Disappearing Faces at the Fairmont Hotel in Mumbai on November 22. The conversation covered ageing, individuality, education, devotion and the changing lifestyles of people living in remote Himalayan regions.

Article Title: West Bengal to be renamed 'Paschim Banga'? Proposal to be tabled in Assembly on Dec 9: CM Suvendu
Article Text:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari

West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday announced that a resolution to rename the state as ‘Paschim Banga’ will be moved in the Assembly on December 9. The state Cabinet approved the proposal at a meeting earlier in the day.Speaking to ANI reporters in Kolkata, Adhikari said the resolution would be introduced during the Assembly’s winter session, scheduled from December 4 to 14. He also clarified that ‘Paschim Banga’ would be the state's name in English.“In English, too, West Bengal will be ‘Paschim Banga’. ‘Paschim Banga’—it must be written exactly as is. We are bringing a resolution to the Legislative Assembly on the 9th; following that, it will go to the Government of India and then to Parliament,” he told the news agency.The chief minister said the proposed change was linked to the state's history and its formation in 1947.“This is a matter of history—the history surrounding the formation of West Bengal, which took place in 1947. This change is something that ought to happen. Instead of ‘West Bengal’, it will be ‘Paschim Banga’,” he added.If passed by the state Assembly, the resolution will be sent to the Centre for approval. The renaming will require clearance from the central government and Parliament before it can formally take effect.The announcement follows remarks by West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya in October, when he indicated that the state would be renamed.
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that a resolution to rename the state as ‘Paschim Banga’ will be moved in the Assembly on December 9. The state Cabinet approved the proposal at a meeting earlier in the day.

Article Title: 'Stop acting like Baahubali': SC raps Bihar judicial officer for FIR against SP for disobeying directions
Article Text:
SC pulled up a Bihar judge for convicting an SP over non-compliance with directions to register an FIR

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday pulled up a Bihar judicial officer for convicting a police officer over non-compliance with directions to register an FIR. The top court questioned his understanding of contempt law and telling him not to "act like a Baahubali" while exercising judicial powers. The bench also suggested that the judicial officer be sent for training to the National Judicial Academy."Ask your client to stop acting like a 'Bahubali' while exercising judicial powers," Chief Justice Surya Kant said while hearing the judicial officer's plea against a Patna high court order staying his decision.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana criticised district and additional sessions judge-IV, Rohtas at Sasaram, Anil Kumar for convicting the police officer on the same day and treating the non-compliance as an offence committed in the face of the court."We are really surprised at your understanding of law. You must first understand the scope and ambit of Section 384 BNSS and Section 345 CrPC. If someone slaps someone or abuses the court, or refuses to leave the courtroom when directed, that is an offence committed in the face of the court. But if we direct someone to register an FIR and they do not, it does not amount to a crime committed in the face of the court," news agency PTI quoted the bench as saying."Your understanding of law is appalling. You also took such an aggressive stance, called the superintendent and convicted him on the same day," Justice Bagchi said.Questioning the judge's objection to an inspecting judge's intervention, Justice Bagchi said, "Were you within your domain and jurisdiction when you called the district magistrate and superintendent of police, treated their non-appearance as an offence committed in the face of the court and convicted and sentenced him? You also stay your hands.Enough of adventure."On September 29, 2026, Anil Kumar convicted IPS officer Raushan Kumar, then superintendent of police (SP) of Rohtas, for wilfully disobeying court directions to register an FIR against a person who had allegedly given false evidence in a criminal case decided in 2023.The judicial officer imposed a symbolic fine of Rs 1 on the SP and directed Bihar's director general of police (DGP) to enter the court's observations into the officer's service records. He also called on the Union ministry of personnel and training to overhaul the training of IAS and IPS officers to better align them with a democratic setup.The Patna high court had subsequently stayed the order imposing the fine on the SP for contempt of court.
Article Summary: The top court questioned his understanding of contempt law and told him not to "act like a Baahubali" while exercising judicial powers. The bench suggested that the judicial officer be sent for training to the National Judicial Academy. On September 29, 2026, Anil Kumar convicted IPS officer Raushan Kumar, then superintendent of police (SP) of Rohtas.

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath penned an emotional letter to his late mother, Savitri Devi , recalling a deeply personal moment from his life as a monk when he returned home in saffron robes to seek alms from her. The letter, published in the latest edition of ‘Mukhyamantri Pati’, comes days after his 91-year-old mother passed away at her native village in Uttarakhand.Savitri Devi died on Friday morning at her ancestral home in Panchur village in Pauri Garhwal district. Her mortal remains were taken to Namami Gange Ghat, also known as Chandi Ghat, in Haridwar on Saturday for the last rites. Adityanath gave a shoulder to his mother's mortal remains and was seen getting emotional as he paid his final respects.Following her death, the chief minister shared a tribute on X, writing: “There is no shade like a mother’s, no refuge like a mother’s. There is no protection like a mother’s, no love like a mother’s.”In his latest letter, written in Hindi and titled ‘Yogi Ki Pati’, Adityanath dedicated his message to mothers and wrote: “This letter is dedicated to every mother, without whom life would not exist. Without mothers, neither you nor I would be here. No living being would have an existence, and this world itself would not exist. A mother is not merely the one who gives birth; she is the mother of the universe.Even God has a mother. ”“Today, once again, my eyes fill with tears as I remember every mother,” Yogi wrote, recalling the blessings of Mata Kaushalya when Lord Ram left for exile and Lord Krishna's journey from the prison in Mathura to Gokul at his mother's wish. “A mother can take the place of anyone, but no one can ever take the place of a mother. A mother's affection is the most beautiful emotion in the world.”The chief minister also recounted an incident from more than three years after he embraced monastic life. Standing outside his home in Panchur in saffron robes, he called out to his mother for alms, as required by the monastic tradition.“Mother, please give me alms,” he recalled saying. His mother, struggling to understand the sight before her, asked: “Son, what have you done to yourself? Is there nothing to eat at home that you have to beg for alms?”Adityanath said he replied: “Mother, renunciation is my duty. A yogi’s hunger can only be satisfied through alms. Mother, I have not come to stay here; I have come to seek alms. Whatever you offer will fulfil my purpose.”In a post on X accompanying the message, Adityanath said the values of Sanatan Dharma were rooted in reverence for mothers. “Some debts can never be repaid. Yes, we can certainly fulfil our duty. Since entering public life, I have been striving to fulfil this duty towards the mothers of our state,” he wrote.“The true mark of respect for every mother would be for every resident of the state to take a pledge today: to become a source of support for a mother without anyone to care for her, to understand the pain of a deprived mother, and to bring a smile to the face of a mother in distress.”The post's accompanying photograph also carried a link to the Uttar Pradesh government's Women and Child Development Department website.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath penned an emotional letter to his late mother, Savitri Devi, recalling a deeply personal moment from his life as a monk. The letter, published in the latest edition of ‘Mukhyamantri Pati’, comes days after his 91-year-old mother passed away.

Article Title: 'Why remove mata Sita's name?' Congress slams BJP over 'Jai Shri Ram' remark

Congress slams BJP over 'Jai Shri Ram' remark

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Ajay Rai on Sunday criticised Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya over his remarks on the slogans 'Jai Shri Ram' and 'Radhe Radhe', accusing the BJP leader of having a "perverted mindset" for dropping the name of Goddess Sita from the traditional greeting."This reflects the perverted mindset of Keshav Prasad Maurya. These are people with a perverted mindset. No one has any problem with the original phrasing. Previously, instead of 'Jai Shri Ram', the phrase used was 'Jai Siya Ram'—but these people have even removed the name of Mother Sita..." Rai said.His remarks came amid a war of words between Maurya and Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav over the BJP's slogan, 'Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De' (May the lotus bloom).On Sunday, Maurya took a swipe at the SP, saying its leaders had earlier felt uneasy hearing 'Jai Shri Ram' and were now troubled even by the chant of 'Radhe Radhe'.In a post on X, Maurya said, “SP leaders earlier felt uneasy hearing ‘Jai Shri Ram’. Now they are troubled even by ‘Radhe Radhe’.”“In Ayodhya, ‘Jai Shri Ram’ resonates, while in Braj people greet each other by saying ‘Radhe Radhe’,” he said.Asking Yadav to clarify his position, the deputy chief minister said, “Does this mean people in Uttar Pradesh will now have to seek his permission before taking the name of their deity?”Maurya accused the SP of indulging in appeasement politics and said both ‘Jai Shri Ram’ and ‘Radhe Radhe’ would continue to resonate in Uttar Pradesh.He also claimed that the party's hopes of returning to power in the 2027 Assembly elections would be dashed and that the BJP would form the government again.The exchange followed Yadav's remarks on Saturday, when he mocked the BJP's slogan during a press conference at the party headquarters in Lucknow.Referring to the slogan coined after the BJP's two-day meeting in Mathura, the former chief minister said the party was aware that its lotus symbol was wilting and was therefore chanting 'Radhe Radhe'.“‘Radhe Radhe’ is said at the time of farewell in our tradition. It means the BJP is going to be shown the door,” Yadav had said, claiming that the people of Uttar Pradesh would give the party a “grand farewell” in the coming elections.On Sunday, responding to Maurya's remarks, Yadav said, "I would never invite him to my house in my lifetime. But you (reporter) are welcome to visit our house; we will show you 'Radhe Radhe'.""'Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De' go ahead and make it bloom. Does it mean the lotus has withered? Why do you (BJP) need to make it bloom again? It has withered," he said at a press conference.Yadav also accused the BJP of selectively invoking religious sentiments, clarifying that his party was not opposed to 'katha' (religious discourses) but objected to controversial remarks about Hindu deities."The Samajwadi Party is not against 'katha'. But what were the views expressed about the father of Lord Shri Ram and what was said about our Lord Krishna? These are the same BJP people who once made Lord Hanuman dance at their programme," he said without naming anyone."Can you make such remarks about Lord Ram's father? Tell me, what would happen if someone among us made such a statement?" he added.
Article Summary: Congress leader Ajay Rai criticised Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya over his remarks on the slogans 'Jai Shri Ram' and 'Radhe Radhe' Rai accused the BJP leader of having a "perverted mindset" for dropping the name of Goddess Sita from the traditional greeting. His remarks came amid a war of words between MauryA and Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav over the BJP's slogan.

Article Title: Shashi Tharoor agrees with PM Modi on corporate tax cuts, then takes a jibe

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Sunday backed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's criticism of corporate leaders for failing to pass on the benefits of reduced corporate taxes to employees through higher salaries and increased hiring.However, he also used the Prime Minister's remarks to take digs at the government over the employment situation, regulatory hurdles and corruption.Reacting to the Prime Minister's remarks, Tharoor said PM Modi had a point in arguing that the government had lowered corporate taxes to encourage companies to invest, create jobs and raise salaries, but businesses had not fulfilled their part of the bargain.“I think what the Prime Minister said is a reality. The corporates may have their own defence of it, but his argument, as I understand it, is that the government has lowered taxes to encourage companies to invest more, create more jobs, and raise salaries, and the companies have not kept their share of the bargain,” Tharoor said.He pointed to the difficulties faced by job seekers, particularly fresh graduates, saying the public had repeatedly raised concerns about the lack of employment opportunities.Citing reports of an IIT graduate failing to secure a placement, he said such instances, which were rarely heard of in the past, suggested that the employment environment for college graduates was “rather grim”.Tharoor also called for simpler regulations and improvements in the ease of doing business, while alleging that corruption had worsened and urging the government to pay greater attention to the economy.“The economy requires attention, and if the Prime Minister is pointing fingers at the companies and the companies want to point fingers at government policies, that's something we can watch,” he said.“We do believe there are things the government could be doing better. They could certainly be simplifying regulations; ease of doing business is not a reality. And I'm sorry to say that corruption, according to every businessman I speak to, is much worse than it's ever been,” he added.Taking a swipe at the government's anti-corruption slogan, Tharoor said, “And this is something which, honestly, the Prime Minister had famously said: 'Na khaunga, na khane dunga.' And now we realize he only meant beef.”Tharoor's remarks came after PM Modi, addressing the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) annual general meeting on Thursday, criticised industry leaders for not translating the benefits of corporate tax cuts into higher employee salaries or additional jobs.Recalling that the basic corporate tax rate had been reduced from 30 per cent in 2014 to 22 per cent, the Prime Minister questioned whether companies had increased salaries or expanded their workforce following the tax relief.“I know you will not clap. I know that very well, because your appetite is so enormous that no matter how much you are given, it is never enough (aapki bhookh itni hai, kitna hi khilao pet bharta hi nahi),” he told the gathering.“Did you increase the salaries of your employees? Did you increase the number of employees? No. The attitude remains: 'Modiji, you do it, we will see',” he said.The Prime Minister also cited the income-tax exemption for individuals earning up to Rs 12 lakh annually, saying the relief had boosted people's purchasing power and consumption. He referred to the government's reduction of GST rates on several products and faster income-tax refunds, which he said had freed up money that would otherwise have remained tied up for months.The remarks came amid fresh demands from the corporate sector for tax concessions in the upcoming Union Budget, with business leaders having submitted their wish list to the finance minister.While highlighting measures taken by the government to improve the business environment, the Prime Minister urged industry leaders to openly suggest further reforms and assured them that the government was willing to consider their proposals.“I have come because I respect you. But your experience with previous govts has been so bitter that I am paying the price for it. This is not that old govt. This is a friendly govt... Without hesitation and without inhibition, write to me openly and tell me what reforms are still needed,” he said.Recalling an interaction with Income Tax Department officials in Gujarat around 2001-02, when he was the chief minister, Modi said he had questioned the approach of treating taxpayers as potential wrongdoers.The Prime Minister also invoked Mahatma Gandhi's message of Swadeshi and self-reliance, questioning why industry leaders still needed to be reminded of the importance of promoting indigenous products and building an Atmanirbhar Bharat.“Imagine, 100 years have passed, but in 1930, Gandhi left us with this message, and today, so many years later, I too have to say the same thing. Is this your success or your failure? Don't listen to me; at least you could have to listen to Gandhi! (Meri mat mano, par Gandhi kih toh mano bhai). He too spoke of Swadeshi before leaving; he too spoke of Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India). And now you have turned 100 years old, yet things remain right where they were . .. Article Title: COP31 ends without climate pact as countries fail to reach consensus over fossil fuel omission and empty finance promises
Article Text:
COP31 failed to reach consensus on the proposed Antalya Pact, COP31 President Murat Kurum said

World staring at climate crisis

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Countries on Sunday failed to reach an agreement at the 31st session of the UN climate conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey as there was no consensus over the cover decision (overarching political and binding outcome) -- a first such instance since 2009 despite stretching into overtime longer than ever before beyond its schedule time to conclude on Friday -- with some countries and groups including EU, Norway and Panama out-rightly objecting to the final deal for not even mentioning a call to transition away from fossil fuels in the text whereas others criticising it for empty climate finance promise. Incidentally, both Turkey and Australia - twin presidencies of this round of climate conference - are fossil fuel producing nations.India while intervening on behalf of the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) expressed the group's concerns flagging the "dilution of the historical responsibility and obligations of developed countries" in the text but stopped short of its outright rejection noting that they are "willing to move forward, and continue to engage" for the sake of multilateralism."Everyone has worked tirelessly, and despite our discomfort with some elements of the text, are willing to move forward, and continue to engage. A constructive approach going forward would be to respect the work we have done and move forward. We are committed to multilateralism and the principles of consensus and we invite our partners to join us as well," said India's key negotiator, Amandeep Garg, additional secretary in the environment ministry, in his intervention.China during the final plenary agreed to what India maintained and even said this in as many words but chose to accept the version of the final text to keep things moving forward."I am deeply disappointed that COP31 has ended without consensus on an overarching outcome. I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands," said the UN secretary-general, Antonio Guterres.The only other time a COP collapsed before 2009 (COP15 in Copenhagen) was COP6 in the Hague in 2000. The COP15 is, however, considered the biggest disappointment in the history of climate negotiations due to its much wider goal where a legally binding climate agreement could not be reached despite much political hype and preparations ahead of it.Though the COP31 accepted a few decisions and even retained an ambitious '35 by 35' electrification goal as a key takeaway, most of the developing countries expressed strong dissatisfaction over the unresolved amount for the adaptation finance and a move of deploying carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) by 2035 that called for wider deployment of CO2 removal technologies. Many countries argued that the CCUS move raises serious questions about the direction of global mitigation efforts.Under the '35 by 35' target, electricity would supply 35% of global final energy consumption by 2035. At present, the share of electricity in global energy consumption is 23%. The move recognizes the need for stronger grids, storage, system flexibility and better energy access, but the text mentions no specific financial commitments for this aspiration. It also ignored the firm commitment of renewable-powered electrification.In India, electricity currently makes up roughly 22% of the country’s total final energy consumption, with the remainder dominated by oil, coal and natural gas. The country has voluntarily moved quite fast on increasing its renewable footprints, way above many developing countries.COP31 even failed to bridge the overall adaptation finance gap, leaving many developing countries extremely disappointed. India, on behalf of the LMDC, too flagged it in the plenary."... our partners have refused to engage on the issue of climate finance across different negotiating rooms. In fact, we were told that despite the increasing needs of developing countries due to a problem that we have not caused, we should not expect our developed country partners to even engage on the issue of climate finance, since it was 'dead in the water'," Garg told the plenary.Many experts consider COP31 a big political failure as it happened amid wars, geopolitical tensions, economic uncertainty and mounting climate risks. Countries across the globe are facing growing pressures over energy security, industrial competitiveness and public finances, while developing nations struggle with rising adaptation costs and increasingly severe climate impacts. They also flagged that the EU failed miserably to take climate leadership in the absence of the USA which under President Donald Trump stepped out from the Paris Agreement.Developed countries, mainly the EU nations, the UK and Japan resisted measurable commitments to fund climate action while the major fossil fuel producing nations including Saudi Arabia and Russia opposed stronger language on transitioning away from oil, gas and coal. The result was a text that found space for an electrification goal and CCUS but not for strong anti-fossil fuel commitments or public finance needed by developing nations.“The COP 31 outcome reflects an abject lack of political ambition and accountability. Despite negotiations extending till Sunday, countries failed to agree on a meaningful commitment to transition away from fossil fuels or to talk about climate security. There is over emphasis on the unknown devil of CCUS which presents a grave concern of untested technology, and serious implications to forest and food security in many parts of the world," said Aarti Khosla, director, Climate Trends.Harjeet Singh, founding director of the Satat Sampada Climate Foundation, said the COP31 failed the people it was meant to protect. "Rich countries refused to put money on the table to help communities prepare for and recover from climate disasters, and handed polluters a free pass instead. No deal is better than a deal that locks in failure. But this cannot become an excuse for more delay: the money and the plan must now come," he said.
Article Summary: There was no consensus over the cover decision (overarching political and binding outcome) for the first time since 2009. Some countries and groups including EU, Norway and Panama out-rightly objected to the final deal for not even mentioning a call to transition away from fossil fuels in the text.

NEW DELHI: India has retained its position among Asia's top three most powerful countries, with its overall power score rising to 40.5 points in 2026, according to a report by the Lowy Institute.The 2026 Asia Power Index also highlights an increasingly contested regional balance, with the gap between the United States and China narrowing largely due to Washington's missteps rather than Beijing's advances. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's regional leadership assessment also improved, with the report placing him second among Asia's regional leaders.Here are the top key findings:The United States and China continue to dominate Asia's power rankings, but the gap between them has narrowed to its lowest level since the index was launched in 2018. The US leads with 78.9 points, followed by China at 73.6 — a difference of just 5.3 points. The gap in military capability has also narrowed to its smallest recorded level.India ranks third with 40.5 points, followed by Japan with 38.6 points, placing both among Asia's major powers.The gap between India's and China's overall power narrowed to its lowest level since the Asia Power Index was first published in 2018, although China's power remains 80% higher than India's.Prime Minister Narendra Modi was also ranked Asia's second-most effective regional leader, behind Chinese President Xi Jinping, improving three places.However, perceptions of his global leadership and strategic ambition declined, with India's muted response to the sinking of an Iranian naval vessel by a US submarine during the Gulf conflict cited as an example of its lower diplomatic profile.India's Diplomatic Influence, however, remained its strongest measure at 70.3 points, slipping only marginally in a year when most countries faltered.India's economic capability score dipped slightly to 26.4 points, with a weakening rupee, changes in the International Monetary Fund's methodology and a nearly $20 billion drop in outbound investment weighing on its relative GDP standing.The United States recorded its steepest-ever decline in diplomatic influence in 2026, with the Trump administration's unilateral foreign policy, trade tariffs and war with Iran eroding its standing across Asia. Washington's strained ties with international institutions, along with President Donald Trump's remarks on arms sales to Taiwan and military exercises with South Korea, further weakened regional confidence in US leadership.The US Diplomatic Influence score fell by six points to 76.7, marking the fourth consecutive year of decline and the biggest single-year drop in the measure since the Asia Power Index was launched in 2018.The 2026 Asia Power Index evaluates 27 countries and territories across 131 indicators covering eight measures of power, including economic and military capability, resilience, diplomatic influence and economic relationships.

NEW DELHI: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Sunday expressed confidence that the Congress would return to power in the state by winning 90 of the 119 Assembly seats in the 2028 elections. Addressing the party's Political Affairs Committee (PAC) meeting in Hyderabad, he said the Congress leadership was preparing a strategy to strengthen the organisation and secure another term in office."Congress will secure 90 seats with one crore votes in the next assembly elections", the CM asserted.Reddy also told the newly-appointed AICC in-charge of party affairs in Telangana, BM Sandeep, that the state Congress should work towards making Rahul Gandhi the prime minister.He said Telangana would contribute 15 Lok Sabha seats to the Congress in the 2029 general elections, provided the total number of constituencies in the state remained at 17."You have to convey our consensus to Kharge ji, Rahul ji and Sonia ji," he told Sandeep.Revanth Reddy targets BRS over 'false propaganda'The chief minister also criticised the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), accusing its leadership of spreading false narratives against the Congress government in an attempt to return to power.Taking a dig at BRS leaders over their recent protest outside the Assembly, where they took off their shirts after being stopped by the police, Reddy said, "BRS leaders took off their shirts outside the Assembly building recently (when they were stopped by police), and now their trousers will be removed.Warns Congress leaders against public criticismAgainst the backdrop of criticism from some ruling party leaders over his government, Reddy warned Congress members against making negative remarks about the government in public."We are closely observing everyone’s behaviour and the way they speak. The party has complete information on what each leader says in public and in private," he said.He added that leaders who remained aligned with the party's position would receive organisational and other posts in due course.Says Congress could have formed government at Centre in 2024Recalling the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Reddy said he had correctly predicted that the BJP would not cross 240 seats.He argued that had the BJP won 25 fewer seats, and the Congress secured 25 more, the Congress would have formed the government at the Centre.Reddy also recalled that former prime minister Indira Gandhi represented Medak in Telangana as a Lok Sabha member when she was assassinated in 1984. He said the state Congress should now resolve to make Rahul Gandhi the prime minister.Government preparing drought action planThe chief minister said the state government would reach out to people directly after the Sankranti festival in January 2027.He also said the government was preparing an action plan to address possible drought conditions caused by the adverse impact of the El Niño phenomenon.Reddy highlighted the welfare schemes being implemented by his government and recalled the challenges faced by Congress workers during the previous BRS regime.
Article Summary: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy expressed confidence that the Congress would return to power in the state by winning 90 of the 119 Assembly seats in the 2028 elections. Reddy also told the newly-appointed AICC in-charge of party affairs in Telangana, BM Sandeep, that the state Congress should work towards making Rahul Gandhi the prime minister.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In a big milestone for the country’s nuclear sector, Kaiga Generating Station Unit-1 (KGS-1) in Karnataka successfully attained criticality early Sunday for the second time, giving a new lease of life to the nuclear power unit that had been taken offline for life-extension work after 25 years of operation. The disclosure was made on Sunday by Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL), the PSU that designs, builds, commissions and operates nuclear power plants across India.A unit attaining criticality means it has reached a self-sustaining, controlled nuclear fission chain reaction inside its reactor core.KGS-1 had reached first criticality on Sept 26, 2000, and had supplied 37,670 million units before it was shut down for refurbishment activities in April last year. The same unit had set a world record for 962 days of continuous operation on Dec 31, 2018, operating at a 99.3% plant load factor, surpassing the previous global record of 940 days held by Heysham II (Unit 8/Reactor 2) in the UK.“The accomplishing this in just 600 days following its shutdown for major refurbishment activities of EMCCR (en-masse coolant channel replacement) and EMFR (en-masse feeder replacement) on April 1, 2025, KGS-1 has set a new fleet-wide benchmark as the first NPCIL reactor to reach criticality in such a short span,” NPCIL said on X on Sunday.It said, “This remarkable success stands as a reflection of extraordinary dedication, technical excellence, and unified teamwork. ”Kaiga generating station has four operational nuclear units totalling 880 MW and two additional units (5 and 6) under construction, adding 1,400 MW and bringing the total planned capacity to 2,280 MW across six units.Kaiga Units-5 & 6 are state-of-the-art, indigenous 700 MW pressurized heavy-water reactors (PHWRs), which incorporate advanced safety features and are among the safest in the world. Three such PHWRs — KAPS-3&4 and RAPP-7 — are successfully operating in the states of Gujarat and Rajasthan respectively. The components and equipment for the project are supplied by domestic industry partners and works are being executed by Indian contractors, aligning with the Atmanirbhar initiatives of the Modi govt.Just days before, in another development, Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) granted permission for the first approach to criticality of Rajasthan atomic power project unit-8 (RAPP-8) at Rawatbhata, following satisfactory completion of safety reviews.
Article Summary: Kaiga Generating Station Unit-1 (KGS-1) in Karnataka successfully attained criticality early Sunday for the second time. A unit attaining criticality means it has reached a self-sustaining, controlled nuclear fission chain reaction inside its reactor core.

NEW DELHI: Easing rules to make naval jobs more attractive, the Indian Navy has allowed Agniveers who opt for a two-year extension after the initial four-year service to get married. The policy relaxation comes just as the first batch of Naval Agniveers — recruited in late 2022 — completes its initial four-year stint this month. The Union Cabinet recently approved a two-year extended service period for Agniveers, officially called ‘Second Tour of Duty’.“Those Agniveers who have completed their four-year initial service period and have opted for the two-year extension will be allowed to marry, though only after completion of their mandatory initial training on joining. The training will be professional and trade specific,” a defence source told TOI. After completing their training, Agniveers can take the entitled leave for marriage purposes, the source said.The marriage provision is currently not available for Naval Agniveers (ages 17.5 to 21) during the initial four-year service period under the Agnipath scheme. “Navy has made the decision on marriage provision and orders have been issued,” the source said. After the Navy, Indian Army and Indian Air Force could follow suit by allowing Agniveers to marry as per their own specifications.On Nov 4, Chief of Defence Staff General N S Raja Subramani announced the ‘Second Tour of Duty’ provision under the Agnipath scheme, increasing Agniveers’ service duty period from four years to six with increased remuneration. Govt has also decided to create a pathway for “all Agniveers to be enrolled as regular soldiers (permanent job)” if they are willing to continue and meet selection criteria. To make the extension lucrative, extended-tenure Agniveers will receive Rs 43,500 per month in the first year of extension and Rs 47,500 per month in the second year (plus applicable allowances), while govt’s Seva Nidhi contribution will rise to 70% during those two years.
Article Summary: The policy relaxation comes just as the first batch of Naval Agniveers — recruited in late 2022 — completes its initial four-year stint this month. The Union Cabinet recently approved a two-year extended service period for Agnives, officially called ‘Second Tour of Duty’

Article Title: 'Haven't been invited to discuss Indus': Pakistani minister dodges question on 'cut off hands' threat
Article Text:
Pakistan minister Musadik Masood Malik said India had not invited him for talks on the Indus Waters Treaty when asked about his earlier threat

What was the 'cut off hands' remark

NEW DELHI: Pakistan 's climate change minister Musadik Masood Malik on Sunday dodged a question about his earlier "cut off hands" threat over the Indus Waters Treaty suspension, saying he had not been invited by India to discuss the issue. Malik, who is attending the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi, also spoke about Islamabad's position on terrorism , saying discussions should be based on evidence.When asked about his earlier warning over the Indus Waters Treaty, Malik said, "When you invite me to discuss the Indus Water Treaty, we will certainly talk about it. You haven't invited me to discuss the Indus Water Treaty at this moment..."Responding to questions on terrorism, Malik said Pakistan was willing to engage in discussions and present evidence."If you are seeking a lasting solution to the issue—rather than merely looking to provoke—then that is how we should proceed...I am offering you a stable, consistent response: whenever discussions take place, they will be based on evidence. I assure you, such discussions will certainly happen...We have stated on many occasions—in various forums—that evidence can be presented bilaterally; we have also suggested that this could be handled multilaterally—you bring your evidence, and we will bring ours..." he said.In October, Malik had warned India over the suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty, saying, "It has already been declared that whoever touches our water, their hands would be cut off."His remarks came after India put the treaty in abeyance following the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack. New Delhi has maintained that the suspension will remain until Pakistan stops supporting terrorism.Prime Minister Narendra Modi had earlier said, "terror and talks cannot go together; water and blood cannot flow together."Pakistan, meanwhile, has been facing water shortages in parts of Sindh and Balochistan, with dwindling irrigation supplies affecting agricultural regions. The crisis has also triggered disputes over water distribution within the country.
Article Summary: Pakistan's climate change minister Musadik Masood Malik dodged a question about his earlier "cut off hands" threat over the Indus Waters Treaty. Malik said he had not been invited by India to discuss the issue. He also spoke about Islamabad's position on terrorism, saying discussions should be based on evidence.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A US commission has claimed that China's backing of Pakistan during Operation Sindoor had complicated Indian operational planning and tied down Indian military resources, advancing China's goal of constraining and suppressing India's rise as a peer competitor in the Indo-Pacific region."India is one of the few powers outside the US alliance system with the scale to materially affect the long-term competition with China. China understands this, and it is actively working to suppress India's rise across multiple domains," said the latest annual report by US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC). USCC is an independent govt agency created by Congress in 2000 to monitor, probe and submit annual reports on national security and economic implications of bilateral trade and defence ties between US and China. According to the report, China's evolving military partnership with Pakistan has made a two-front contingency an increasingly critical concern for India. "May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict demonstrated how China could strengthen Pakistan during a crisis without Beijing entering the fighting directly, adding to India's concerns about how a future conflict with Pakistan could develop," it said.The USCC report said India’s dependence on Chinese manufacturing has become a key source of leverage for Beijing — and a growing vulnerability for the US.“China has restricted industrial inputs, equipment, technology and expertise to India and required some Indian firms to certify that Chinesesupplied goods would not be reexported to the US. Chinese pricing has also undercut new Indian pharmaceutical production, illustrating Beijing’s intent to undermine Indian suppliers that can compete with established Chinese producers,” it said, adding these dependencies complicate US efforts to diversify supply chains away from China by shifting production to India.It said China’s expanding naval and surveillance presence is beginning to erode India’s longstanding strategic advantages in the Indian Ocean and place additional demands on Indian forces. It said China is beginning to bring its South China Sea playbook to the Indian Ocean, renaming undersea features in ways that could lay the groundwork for potential claims of jurisdiction.
Article Summary: US panel report says China is using military, maritime and economic pressure to constrain India's rise, while strengthening its support for Pakistan. India is one of the few powers outside the US alliance system with the scale to materially affect the long-term competition with China.

Article Title: Bangladesh unrest: Bengal CM Suvendu to write to EAM, may push to extend minority entry cut-off
Article Text:

Bengal BJP chief calls for protests

Political violence escalates in Bangladesh

NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday said he would contact external affairs minister S Jaishankar on Monday to convey concerns in the state over the escalating violence in Bangladesh. He also indicated that the government could seek an extension of the cut-off date for religious minorities fleeing the neighbouring country to enter India.Suvendu said the developments in Bangladesh were "extremely painful" and had caused widespread concern in West Bengal, where many people have relatives across the border. He said the state government could also write to the Centre to seek an extension of the December 31, 2024 cut-off date for religious minorities entering India from Bangladesh, if required."Photographs and videos are coming in, and I am receiving phone calls. People are very worried. Around two crore people in Bengal have relatives there, and the developments are having an impact here as well. If required, we will write to the Centre to extend the timeline," he told reporters.The chief minister said he would speak to Jaishankar after his office opened on Monday and apprise him of the public reaction in West Bengal."As the chief minister of a state, I cannot comment directly on foreign affairs. There is a protocol. I will contact S Jaishankar after the office opens tomorrow and write to him, if required, to apprise him of the reaction here," he said.Suvendu said he had stood by the people of Bangladesh when he was in the Opposition. However, he said his position as the administrative head of a state placed certain limitations on what he could say or do."I also have some limitations. I cannot speak or act without restraint," he said.He did not specify how the unrest in Bangladesh had affected West Bengal.The chief minister's remarks come amid concerns over the safety of religious minorities in Bangladesh and the possibility of people fleeing to India.Under the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) Order, 2025, as amended in November 2026, religious minorities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who entered India by December 31, 2024, fleeing religious persecution, are exempt from entry-document requirements. However, they must obtain an appropriate visa to continue staying in the country.Suvendu indicated that the state could approach the Centre to extend this deadline if the situation warranted it.Meanwhile, West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya urged people to set aside political differences and organise protests against the violence in Bangladesh."As a Bengali Hindu, I appeal to everyone to rise above politics, build resistance and take to the streets. Protests should be held across the world because those being killed are our brothers," he said.Bhattacharya said the Centre would take appropriate decisions on the situation but maintained that people should raise their voices against the attacks.He also said he believed in the idea of "one nation" and argued that the Partition along religious lines had contributed to the present situation.The remarks come amid escalating political violence in Bangladesh, where supporters of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and the banned Awami League clashed in several areas. The clashes prompted the deployment of hundreds of additional paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel.The developments came as Jamaat-e-Islami, the main parliamentary opposition party, launched a 40-day nationwide protest on Saturday. The protest coincided with the planned return of deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina from India next month, despite her death sentence.
Article Summary: Suvendu Adhikari indicated that the state could approach the Centre to extend this deadline for visa extension of religious minorities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan. He said he would contact external affairs minister S Jaishankar on Monday to convey concerns in the state.

Article Title: Help just a call away? How emergency system responds in race against time
Article Text:
What happens after that call is made?

Ambulance Services in India – Are the Sirens Loud Enough!

The first response: What should you do when an emergency strikes?

The gap in calling and receiving the help

Are India's ambulances and emergency services adequately equipped?

Are emergency helplines working when people need them most?

Ambulance availability

Covid exposed the gaps: What India has learnt?

What needs to change

“Repeated calls went unanswered,” recalls Kishan, describing his family's experience during a medical emergency involving his parents.A medical emergency rarely comes with a warning. A sudden cardiac arrest, a road accident or a stroke can turn an ordinary day into a race against time, where every passing minute can mean the difference between life and death. In such moments, one call for help is often the first and most critical step.But what happens after that call is made?From the moment someone dials 108 or 112 to the ambulance reaching the patient and transporting them to a hospital, multiple layers of emergency response are expected to work seamlessly. The call must be answered, an ambulance dispatched, first responders equipped to handle the crisis and hospitals prepared to provide immediate treatment.Yet, delays at any stage can cost a patient their chance of survival.The 2022 review articleby Sonali Randhawa and Sunil Nandraj estimates that approximately 24,012 people die every day in India due to delays in receiving timely medical assistance.The term 'golden hour' is often used in emergency medicine to describe the importance of getting patients appropriate treatment quickly.But the urgency can be even greater in some conditions.“In a cardiac arrest, the chance of survival falls steeply with every minute that passes without CPR,” says Dr Rajiv Jain, HOD and consultant – Emergency Medicine, Gleneagles BGS Hospital. In a heart attack, delays can cause further damage to the heart muscle, while a stroke requires timely treatment to reduce the risk of lasting brain injury.He adds that in trauma cases, studies suggest only about 20% of accident victims reach medical care within the golden hour. Delays can affect not just survival but also the extent of disability a patient may face.Calling an ambulance early is important because trained crews can begin treatment during the journey and alert the hospital before arrival.Knowing what to do while waiting for professional help can make a crucial difference.Dr Jain says the first step is to stay calm, call emergency services and clearly communicate the location and nature of the emergency. The caller should put the phone on speaker so that the operator can guide them.“If they aren't, start chest compressions at once. Push hard and fast in the centre of the chest, at about 100 to 120 compressions a minute, and keep going until help arrives or the person starts to respond,” he says, referring to a person who is unresponsive and not breathing normally.For heavy bleeding, firm pressure should be applied to the wound. An accident victim should not be moved unnecessarily, particularly if a spinal injury is suspected. Food or water should never be given to an unconscious person.“Those first five minutes belong to the bystander, and they often decide the outcome,” Dr Jain says.But what happens if help arrives late?India has expanded its emergency ambulance network, but how effectively does it function when lives are on the line? Recent incidents from across the country have once again raised questions about the reliability of emergency transport.In Madhya Pradesh's Mandla, a young man struggling to breathe died after a government ambulance allegedly ran out of oxygen.In Kalyan, a 70-year-old man with chest pain died outside a railway station, with his family alleging that the 108 ambulance took around 40 minutes to arrive.In Odisha, the family of a critically ill man alleged that the ambulance transporting him from Cuttack to a private facility in Bhubaneswar stopped on a bridge because it had run out of fuel.While the circumstances differ, these incidents point to a common concern: a delay or failure at any stage of emergency transport can put an already vulnerable patient at greater risk.According to Dr Jain, delays are often caused by a combination of factors: traffic, difficulty locating the patient, lack of advance communication with the hospital, registration queues and waiting for a specialist.“The right hospital matters as much as the nearest one,” he says, adding that sending a patient to a facility without the required treatment can lead to further delays.Dr Anshul Kumar Jain, Director – Cardiology, CK Birla Hospital, Delhi, also stresses the importance of choosing a hospital that can provide immediate stabilisation and life-saving treatment. It may not always be necessary to travel to a bigger hospital if an appropriately equipped facility is closer.India has multiple emergency numbers, including 108 and 112. The latter brings police, fire and ambulance services under one platform. However, the time taken by a first responder to reach a location should not be confused with the time taken by a medically equipped ambulance to arrive.The 2022 review article also mentions that the recommended ambulance-to-population ratio is one road ambulance for every 1 lakh people in the plains and one for every 70,000 people in hilly and tribal areas.However, assessing India's actual ambulance availability remains difficult, as government data from different sources appears inconsistent. The availability of ambulances also does not automatically mean that patients will receive the required level of care.The review cites a 2018 assessment by Centralised Accident and Trauma Services (CATS) Delhi, which found that out of 265 state-run ambulances, only 31 had advanced life support facilities such as defibrillators and ventilators. Around 60 were non-operational due to mechanical faults, while nearly 155 were more than six years old.Dr Rajiv Jain says India's ambulance coverage may appear close to international benchmarks on paper, but vehicles are unevenly distributed and many are basic life support ambulances rather than advanced life support vehicles.During the second wave of Covid-19 in 2021, the demand for private ambulances in Delhi increased fivefold compared with previous months, amid a shortage of adequately equipped public ambulances. Private ambulance operators also charged higher rates, according to the review.The gap between having an emergency helpline and getting timely assistance is also reflected in Delhi's ambulance services.A CAG audit recorded 49 instances in February 2020 when CATS ambulances refused emergency calls. Reasons included a lack of staff, unavailability of oxygen and vehicles being unfit to drive.The Delhi government's 2024-25 annual report, meanwhile, recorded an average CATS ambulance response time of 16.91 minutes.The growing use of app-based ambulance services has also brought the issue into focus. Blinkit ambulances have featured in accounts of people turning to private platforms when conventional options appeared slow or unavailable.In one instance reported in November 2026, a Delhi man said he opted for a Blinkit ambulance after waiting for a response to his call to 112 during his grandmother's medical emergency. The ambulance reportedly reached his home in eight minutes.In another case, a woman said her family struggled to arrange a cab during an early-morning emergency involving her aunt, who had suffered a seizure. They eventually booked a free ambulance through Blinkit.The Covid-19 pandemic exposed how quickly emergency healthcare systems can become overwhelmed when demand rises sharply. Ambulances, hospital beds and oxygen became difficult to access, while families struggled to identify facilities that could admit patients.“Covid showed that our system was built for routine demand, not for a surge. Oxygen, beds and ambulances all became scarce at the same time,” says Dr Rajiv Jain.Dr Anshul Kumar Jain says the pandemic showed that emergency healthcare cannot function as a collection of independent hospitals and ambulance providers. It needs to operate as a coordinated network, where ambulance crews can identify which hospital has the required facilities and capacity before transporting a patient.Recalling her family's experience during the Covid-19 pandemic, Kishan, a Delhi resident, said arranging an ambulance during a medical emergency was a major challenge.“Repeated calls went unanswered as the lines remained busy, putting the patient's life at risk.”“It is the responsibility of the authorities to ensure that emergency helpline numbers remain functional and accessible to everyone, especially during a crisis. It is their failure when they cannot provide even basic facilities inside an ambulance. There was no bed inside the ambulance. We keep coming across reports of patients losing their lives because essential facilities are not made available in time. These delays can prove fatal,” he said.For Dr Jain, improving emergency response requires more than adding ambulances.The system needs quicker dispatch, trained crews, advance alerts to hospitals, real-time information on facilities and clear accountability when delays occur.“What we need now is accountability: published response times, GPS-tagged ambulances, hospital capability grading, trauma registries, and a review of every preventable death as a system failure, not just bad luck,” he says. “When a life is lost in transit, the question must be what failed, not who was unlucky.”Dr Harshitha Sridhar, HOD and Consultant – Emergency Medicine, Manipal Hospital Millers Road, says strengthening the culture of first responders is equally important.“We also need to strengthen the culture of first responders. Police personnel, traffic police, security guards, teachers, public transport staff and even ordinary citizens should receive basic CPR and first-aid training.“India needs to move from a predominantly ambulance-transport model to a prehospital emergency medical care model. An effective emergency response system must be capable of saving lives before a patient reaches the hospital.”For Kishan, who lost a family member, the experience remains a reminder of how helpless families can feel when every minute matters.He suggests people to keep emergency contacts handy and ensure that family members are prepared to act quickly.“Family members should also know how to drive, preferably more than one person. During an emergency, we cannot always depend on ambulances to arrive on time,” he says.An emergency call should bring assistance, not leave them waiting and wondering if help will arrive in time.
Article Summary: India has expanded its emergency ambulance network, but how effectively does it function when lives are on the line? Recent incidents from across the country have once again raised questions about the reliability of emergency transport. Approximately 24,012 people die every day in India due to delays in receiving timely medical assistance.

Article Title: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri over unsafe packaged drinking water
Article Text:
FSSAI sanctions action against Bisleri International.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) on Sunday sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd after a sample of its packaged drinking water was found unsafe.In a social media post, the food safety regulator said a sample of "Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)" collected from Bisleri's premises was found to be non-compliant with prescribed safety standards."The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," FSSAI said.The company subsequently appealed against the findings, following which the sample was sent to a referral food laboratory for further analysis.The laboratory also declared it "unsafe" after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the regulator said.Based on the laboratory findings, FSSAI concluded that the company had violated provisions relating to unsafe food under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. It has, therefore, sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd under the law.Apart from Bisleri, the regulator also sanctioned prosecution against several other companies, including Vasant Masala Pvt Ltd, Tit-Bit Foods India Pvt Ltd, Mimansa Industries and Asha Confectionery.FSSAI also suspended the licences of Urmi Lifesciences LLP and Gaur Ayurvedic Store for non-compliance with food safety rules and regulations, news agency PTI reported.The latest action comes amid an intensified enforcement drive by FSSAI against food business operators (FBOs) and e-commerce companies during the current calendar year. The regulator has also stepped up scrutiny of energy drink and alcoholic beverage manufacturers.One of its recent regulatory disputes involves the classification of Red Bull as an "energy drink". In June, FSSAI moved against the use of the label, raising concerns that the high added-sugar content of certain beverages could mislead consumers and encourage excessive consumption.Red Bull, PepsiCo, Monster Beverage and Reliance Consumer challenged the regulator's order in the Delhi high court, arguing that the restrictions were imposed without giving them prior notice.Red Bull subsequently secured an interim court injunction allowing it to continue using the "energy drink" label. Its competitors, however, were directed to stop using the classification after exhausting their existing stocks.FSSAI has challenged the relief granted to Red Bull, arguing that it gives the company "an undue commercial advantage" over its rivals. The matter is scheduled to be heard in January.
Article Summary: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India sanctions prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd. The regulator says a sample of its packaged drinking water was found unsafe. The company appealed against the findings, following which the sample was sent to a referral food laboratory for further analysis.
